title: be stopped meds, but home didn't consult MD - Winnipeg Free Press
subtitle: Breaking News, Sports, Manitoba, Canada
article: This article was published 08/04/2011 (5259 days ago), so information in it may no longer be current.
A mentally ill Winnipeg man stopped taking his medication several weeks before he stabbed a fellow care-home patient to death, triggering a police shooting that killed him.

New details about the March 2007 tragedy have emerged at a provincial inquest, which ended Thursday with lawyers saying little could have been done to prevent the tragedy. A provincial court judge will release a report later this year which may include suggestions on how to prevent future incidents.

Ahmed Saleh-Azad, 61, died after being shot by police officers responding to a call for help inside Madison Memorial Lodge on Evanson Street, a non-profit housing service for seniors, addicts, recently paroled prisoners and the elderly.

A blood-spattered Saleh-Azad refused to drop his knife after stabbing Alexander Kolesnyk, 57, inside the facility cafeteria moments earlier. Kolesnyk was pronounced dead at the scene of what lawyers described as "catastrophic" injuries.
Kim Carswell, a lawyer for the Winnipeg Police Service, told court the entire deadly encounter lasted only a few short minutes.

"We need to be very careful about trying to parse these seconds down and judging those officers who had to make decisions in that period of time," she said Thursday in her final argument to the court. Carswell noted much of the violence was captured on surveillance video and shows Saleh-Azad calmly sitting down at a table after killing Kolesnyk, then advancing toward police as soon as they arrive.
"The last image you see in the video (before he leaves the frame) is of his hand with the knife coming up," said Carswell.
Saleh-Azad had a history of violent and bizarre behaviour and was sent to the facility in 2005 after a brief stint in hospital, court was told.

In 2005, Saleh-Azad was charged with three counts of assault, assaulting a peace officer, and one count of breaching a recognizance order by failing to keep the peace after he spat at a provincial court judge, two defence lawyers and a sheriff's officer in the courtroom. At the time, Saleh-Azad was facing charges of assault but had not yet been called to court.

Saleh-Azad was doing well at the facility but his behaviour began to deteriorate in early 2007 when he assaulted a home-care aide who was coming to the facility on a regular basis to ensure he was taking his medication, court was told. He also committed a similar attack against a community health worker who would take him to various medical appointments.

An internal decision was made in February 2007 to stop sending home care because of safety fears, and shortly after Saleh-Azad stopped taking his medication, according to several witnesses who testified at the inquest. The decision was made by staff at the facility without consultation with Saleh-Azad's doctor.
It was only a few weeks later that he randomly attacked Kolesnyk with a knife, triggering the police response which ended with his own death.
